name: 40283-videoprompt-12b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1).
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1. One in-process engine (guidellm `vllm_python`), no router, no external cache tier.
architecture: C-RADIOv2-H ViT-H/16 vision tower over a 12B hybrid Mamba2/attention decoder (62 layers: 6 attention, 56 Mamba2), bf16, ~24.6 GiB of weights. Full geometry is in the checkpoint's own config.json.
load_profile: concurrent (CLOSED loop), streams=2, warmup the first 20% by completion, bounded at 40 requests with a 480 s safety cap. The count is small because the load generator, not the engine, sets the pace: guidellm synthesises a fresh 512-frame clip per request in a single data-loader process at roughly 21 CPU-seconds each, so a request arrives about every 10-13 s and a longer bound buys wall-clock rather than samples.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_video` + `synthetic_text` zipped into one request: one 512-frame 512x512 mp4 clip (h264, gradient, fps 1.0, seed 42) and one 32-token instruction, answered in exactly 128 greedy tokens. A different clip on every request. The clip expands to roughly 47k prompt tokens per request, not 32 -- that is the model's own token budget for 512 frames, not drift.
purpose: A video question-answering assistant captioning minute-long clips with short instructions, two concurrent users, one GPU.
launch:
# Engine config for 40283-videoprompt-12b-1gpu. Interpreter and hardware live in configs/env.yaml.
model: nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-12B-v2-VL-BF16
trust-remote-code: true
tensor-parallel-size: 1
dtype: bfloat16

# ALL 512 FRAMES, NOT THE DEFAULT 32. vLLM's video reader samples 32 frames out of whatever clip
# arrives unless num_frames says otherwise, so without this line the 512-frame clip declared in
# scenario.json is silently reduced to 32 and the served workload is not the declared one.
media-io-kwargs: {"video": {"num_frames": 512}}

# THE CHECKPOINT'S OWN PRUNING RATE, WHICH vLLM DOES NOT INHERIT. The HF config declares
# video_pruning_rate 0.7, but MultiModalConfig.video_pruning_rate defaults to None
# (vllm/config/multimodal.py) and is never read from the checkpoint -- it arrives only via this
# engine arg. With it unset, Efficient Video Sampling is off and a 512-frame clip expands to
# 512*256 = 131072 video embeddings plus ~10k of per-frame scaffolding = 141140 tokens, which
# exceeds max-model-len; every request is then rejected at admission with "decoder prompt is
# longer than the maximum model length" and the run exits rc=0 having served nothing.
# With it set, compute_retained_tokens_count gives int(131072*0.3) = 39321 retained embeddings,
# i.e. the ~47k prompt tokens this item declares and that max-model-len 65536 was sized on.
video-pruning-rate: 0.7

limit-mm-per-prompt: {"image": 0, "video": 1}
mm-processor-cache-gb: 0
max-model-len: 65536
max-num-batched-tokens: 65536
max-num-seqs: 16
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90
